evidence.V1: Top view reads clearly as a plank floor, but front/three-quarter/silhouette read as a plain 2-stud-deep box with tiny bumps on top (a crate/plinth rather than a floor).
evidence.V2: Medium planks and small nail dots exist, but the big mass is an unarticulated deep base block that takes over half the read; only 4 nails on 9 planks.
evidence.V3: Chunky planks are pleasantly stylised, but the tall slab base under them is a stiff primitive and makes the floor piece read thick and boxy.
evidence.V4: Planks have consistent chamfers that catch light (edge close-up), but the base box edges look near-razor with no visible bevel - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (studio and flat) clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting; gap lines between planks crisp. Gates A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: One wood hue in ~3 values (light, mid, dark base) plus ink nails; colourways (walnut, teal) hold the same disciplined value structure.
evidence.V7: 396 tris vs module target 800 - well under.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor white material, wood hue as specified for plank floors, but unchamfered base box breaks the kit's chamfered-edge rule.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a modular piece: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling passes with IoU 1.0 on X and Y.

artifacts: planks overhang the base box slightly, leaving a visible lip/step around the top rim in front view (designed, but reads like a lid on a box)
top_fixes: Reduce the base depth or break it up (joists/beams, darker recessed underside) so the piece reads as a floor, not a crate
Add 0.05-0.07 stud chamfers to the base box edges to match the planks and kit
Make the plank layout more regular (consistent running bond) and add nails to more planks for small-scale detail
